sanskrit: pratijajñe ca kākutsthaḥ samare vālino vadham sugrīvaś cāpi vaidehyāḥ punar ānayanaṃ nṛpa
english: The scion of Kakutstha pledged to slay Valin in battle, O king, and Sugriva in turn pledged to bring back the daughter of Videha.

sanskrit: ity uktvā samayaṃ kṛtvā viśvāsya ca parasparam abhyetya sarve kiṣkindhāṃ tasthur yuddhābhikāṅkṣiṇaḥ
english: Having spoken thus and made their compact, placing mutual trust in one another, they all approached Kishkindha and stood there eager for battle.

sanskrit: sugrīvaḥ prāpya kiṣkindhāṃ nanādaughanibhasvanaḥ nāsya tan mamṛṣe vālī taṃ tārā pratyaṣedhayat
english: Sugriva, reaching Kishkindha, roared with a sound like a thunder-cloud. Valin did not tolerate that, but Tara tried to restrain him.

sanskrit: yathā nadati sugrīvo balavān eṣa vānaraḥ manye cāśrayavān prāpto na tvaṃ nirgantum arhasi
english: "As Sugriva roars like this, this mighty monkey must have come with a powerful protector—you should not go out."

sanskrit: hemamālī tato vālī tārāṃ tārādhipānanām provāca vacanaṃ vāgmī tāṃ vānarapatiḥ patiḥ
english: Then Valin, lord of monkeys, he who wears a golden garland, eloquent of speech, spoke to Tara, whose face was like the lord of stars.

sanskrit: sarvabhūtarutajñā tvaṃ paśya buddhyā samanvitā kenāpāśrayavān prāpto mamaiṣa bhrātṛgandhikaḥ
english: "You who understand the cries of all creatures, consider carefully with your wisdom: by whose support has this one who resembles my brother come here?"

sanskrit: cintayitvā muhūrtaṃ tu tārā tārādhipaprabhā patim ity abravīt prājñā śṛṇu sarvaṃ kapīśvara
english: Having reflected for a moment, Tara, radiant as the lord of stars, spoke wisely to her husband: "Hear everything, O lord of monkeys."

sanskrit: hṛtadāro mahāsattvo rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ tulyārimitratāṃ prāptaḥ sugrīveṇa dhanurdharaḥ
english: "Rama, son of Dasharatha, great-souled and a master of the bow, whose wife has been carried off, has entered into an alliance with Sugriva as an equal."

sanskrit: bhrātā cāsya mahābāhuḥ saumitrir aparājitaḥ lakṣmaṇo nāma medhāvī sthitaḥ kāryārthasiddhaye
english: "His brother too, the mighty-armed and unconquered son of Sumitra, the wise Lakshmana, stands ready to accomplish their purpose."

sanskrit: maindaś ca dvividaś caiva hanūmāṃś cānilātmajaḥ jāmbavān ṛkṣarājaś ca sugrīvasacivāḥ sthitāḥ
english: "Mainda and Dvivida, Hanuman son of the Wind, Jambavan king of bears—all of Sugriva's ministers stand with him."

sanskrit: sarva ete mahātmāno buddhimanto mahābalāḥ alaṃ tava vināśāya rāmavīryavyapāśrayāt
english: "All these great souls, wise and mighty, relying on the valour of Rama, are more than enough to bring about your destruction."

sanskrit: tasyās tad ākṣipya vaco hitam uktaṃ kapīśvaraḥ paryaśaṅkata tām īrṣuḥ sugrīvagatamānasām
english: The lord of monkeys dismissed her well-meaning words and, filled with jealousy, suspected her heart of being set upon Sugriva.

sanskrit: tārāṃ paruṣam uktvā sa nirjagāma guhāmukhāt sthitaṃ mālyavato 'bhyāśe sugrīvaṃ so 'bhyabhāṣata
english: Having spoken harshly to Tara, he went out from the mouth of the cave and addressed Sugriva, who stood near mount Malyavat.

sanskrit: asakṛt tvaṃ mayā mūḍha nirjito jīvitapriyaḥ mukto jñātir iti jñātvā kā tvarā maraṇe punaḥ
english: "Fool, you have been defeated by me more than once, and spared because you clung to life—I let you go knowing you were a kinsman. What haste is this to die again?"

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ prāha sugrīvo bhrātaraṃ hetumad vacaḥ prāptakālam amitraghno rāmaṃ saṃbodhayann iva
english: Thus addressed, Sugriva, slayer of foes, replied to his brother with reasoned words fitting the moment, as though prompting Rama.

sanskrit: hṛtadārasya me rājan hṛtarājyasya ca tvayā kiṃ nu jīvitasāmarthyam iti viddhi samāgatam
english: "O king, my wife has been taken by you and my kingdom stripped away—know then that I have come, for what worth is a life so diminished?"

sanskrit: evam uktvā bahuvidhaṃ tatas tau saṃnipetatuḥ samare vālisugrīvau śālatālaśilāyudhau
english: Having spoken at length in this manner, the two of them then fell upon one another in battle—Valin and Sugriva, armed with sala-trees, palm-trees, and rocks.

sanskrit: ubhau jaghnatur anyonyam ubhau bhūmau nipetatuḥ ubhau vavalgatuś citraṃ muṣṭibhiś ca nijaghnatuḥ
english: Both struck each other, both fell to the ground, both leapt up again wonderfully, and both struck with their fists.

sanskrit: ubhau rudhirasaṃsiktau nakhadantaparikṣatau śuśubhāte tadā vīrau puṣpitāv iva kiṃśukau
english: Both drenched in blood, both lacerated by nails and teeth, those two heroes shone at that moment like two flowering kimsuka trees.

sanskrit: na viśeṣas tayor yuddhe tadā kaś cana dṛśyate sugrīvasya tadā mālāṃ hanūmān kaṇṭha āsajat
english: No distinction between the two could be discerned in battle at that time; so Hanuman placed a garland around Sugriva's neck as a mark.

sanskrit: sa mālayā tadā vīraḥ śuśubhe kaṇṭhasaktayā śrīmān iva mahāśailo malayo meghamālayā
english: The hero then shone with the garland hanging about his neck like the great and splendid mount Malaya garlanded by a wreath of clouds.

sanskrit: kṛtacihnaṃ tu sugrīvaṃ rāmo dṛṣṭvā mahādhanuḥ vicakarṣa dhanuḥśreṣṭhaṃ vālim uddiśya lakṣyavat
english: Seeing Sugriva thus marked, Rama of the great bow drew back his supreme bow and took aim at Valin as at a target.

sanskrit: visphāras tasya dhanuṣo yantrasyeva tadā babhau vitatrāsa tadā vālī śareṇābhihato hṛdi
english: The twang of his bow resounded then like a great mechanical contrivance; and Valin, struck to the heart by the arrow, was terrified.

sanskrit: sa bhinnamarmābhihato vaktrāc choṇitam udvaman dadarśāvasthitaṃ rāmam ārāt saumitriṇā saha
english: His vital points pierced and struck, vomiting blood from his mouth, he saw Rama standing nearby together with the son of Sumitra.

sanskrit: garhayitvā sa kākutsthaṃ papāta bhuvi mūrchitaḥ tārā dadarśa taṃ bhūmau tārāpatim iva cyutam
english: Having censured the scion of Kakutstha, he fell senseless to the earth; and Tara saw him lying on the ground like the lord of stars fallen from heaven.

sanskrit: hate vālini sugrīvaḥ kiṣkindhāṃ pratyapadyata tāṃ ca tārāpatimukhīṃ tārāṃ nipatiteśvarām
english: With Valin slain, Sugriva returned to Kishkindha and to Tara, whose face was like the moon, whose lord had fallen.

sanskrit: rāmas tu caturo māsān pṛṣṭhe mālyavataḥ śubhe nivāsam akarod dhīmān sugrīveṇābhyupasthitaḥ
english: Wise Rama then dwelt for four months on the auspicious slopes of mount Malyavat, attended upon by Sugriva.

sanskrit: rāvaṇo 'pi purīṃ gatvā laṅkāṃ kāmabalātkṛtaḥ sītāṃ niveśayām āsa bhavane nandanopame aśokavanikābhyāśe tāpasāśramasaṃnibhe
english: Ravana too, going to the city of Lanka, impelled by the force of desire, lodged Sita in a palace like Nandana, near the Ashoka grove, which resembled the hermitage of an ascetic.

sanskrit: bhartṛsmaraṇatanvaṅgī tāpasīveṣadhāriṇī upavāsatapaḥśīlā tatra sā pṛthulekṣaṇā uvāsa duḥkhavasatīḥ phalamūlakṛtāśanā
english: Slender from constant remembrance of her husband, clad in an ascetic's garb, given to fasting and austerity, that wide-eyed one dwelt there in miserable abode, living on fruits and roots.

sanskrit: dideśa rākṣasīs tatra rakṣaṇe rākṣasādhipaḥ prāsāsiśūlaparaśumudgarālātadhāriṇīḥ
english: The lord of rakshasas posted rakshasis there to guard her, wielding lances, swords, spears, axes, clubs, and firebrands.

sanskrit: dvyakṣīṃ tryakṣīṃ lalāṭākṣīṃ dīrghajihvām ajihvikām tristanīm ekapādāṃ ca trijaṭām ekalocanām
english: Two-eyed, three-eyed, forehead-eyed, long-tongued, tongueless, three-breasted, one-footed, Trijata, and one-eyed—

sanskrit: etāś cānyāś ca dīptākṣyaḥ karabhotkaṭamūrdhajāḥ parivāryāsate sītāṃ divārātram atandritāḥ
english: these and others besides, with blazing eyes and hair as thick as an elephant's trunk, surrounded Sita day and night without rest.

sanskrit: tās tu tām āyatāpāṅgīṃ piśācyo dāruṇasvanāḥ tarjayanti sadā raudrāḥ paruṣavyañjanākṣarāḥ
english: Those she-demons, terrible in voice, fearsome, speaking harsh and grating syllables, constantly menaced that long-eyed one.

sanskrit: khādāma pāṭayāmaināṃ tilaśaḥ pravibhajya tām yeyaṃ bhartāram asmākam avamanyeha jīvati
english: "Let us eat her, tear her apart, divide her into pieces—she who dares to dishonour our master and yet lives!"

sanskrit: ity evaṃ paribhartsantīs trāsyamānā punaḥ punaḥ bhartṛśokasamāviṣṭā niḥśvasyedam uvāca tāḥ
english: As they threatened her thus, frightening her again and again, she, overcome by grief for her husband, heaved a sigh and spoke to them.

sanskrit: āryāḥ khādata māṃ śīghraṃ na me lobho 'sti jīvite vinā taṃ puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ nīlakuñcitamūrdhajam
english: "Noble ladies, eat me quickly—I have no desire for life without that lotus-eyed one with dark, curling hair."

sanskrit: apy evāhaṃ nirāhārā jīvitapriyavarjitā śoṣayiṣyāmi gātrāṇi vyālī tālagatā yathā
english: "Even so, I, without food and freed from any love of life, will wither my limbs like a serpent coiled around a palm tree."

sanskrit: na tv anyam abhigaccheyaṃ pumāṃsaṃ rāghavād ṛte iti jānīta satyaṃ me kriyatāṃ yad anantaram
english: "I will never approach any man other than the son of Raghu—know this as truth; do with me whatever comes next."

sanskrit: tasyās tad vacanaṃ śrutvā rākṣasyas tāḥ kharasvanāḥ ākhyātuṃ rākṣasendrāya jagmus tat sarvam āditaḥ
english: Hearing those words of hers, those harsh-voiced rakshasis went to report everything from the beginning to the lord of rakshasas.

sanskrit: gatāsu tāsu sarvāsu trijaṭā nāma rākṣasī sāntvayām āsa vaidehīṃ dharmajñā priyavādinī
english: When all of them had gone, a rakshasi named Trijata, learned in righteousness and speaking kind words, consoled the daughter of Videha.

sanskrit: sīte vakṣyāmi te kiṃ cid viśvāsaṃ kuru me sakhi bhayaṃ te vyetu vāmoru śṛṇu cedaṃ vaco mama
english: "Sita, I will tell you something—place your trust in me, my friend; let your fear depart, O fair-thighed one; hear these words of mine."

sanskrit: avindhyo nāma medhāvī vṛddho rākṣasapuṃgavaḥ sa rāmasya hitānveṣī tvadarthe hi sa māvadat
english: "There is a wise and aged foremost rakshasa named Avindhya, a well-wisher of Rama; he spoke to me on your behalf."

sanskrit: sītā madvacanād vācyā samāśvāsya prasādya ca bhartā te kuśalī rāmo lakṣmaṇānugato balī
english: "'Tell Sita in my words, after comforting and reassuring her: your husband Rama is well, mighty, and accompanied by Lakshmana.'"

sanskrit: sakhyaṃ vānararājena śakrapratimatejasā kṛtavān rāghavaḥ śrīmāṃs tavdarthe ca samudyataḥ
english: "The illustrious son of Raghu has made alliance with the king of monkeys, whose splendour rivals Indra, and is fully exerting himself on your behalf."

sanskrit: mā ca te 'stu bhayaṃ bhīru rāvaṇāl lokagarhitāt nalakūbaraśāpena rakṣitā hy asy anindite
english: "Let there be no fear in you, timid one, from Ravana who is condemned by the world—for you are protected by the curse of Nalakubara, O blameless one."

sanskrit: śapto hy eṣa purā pāpo vadhūṃ rambhāṃ parāmṛśan na śakto vivaśāṃ nārīm upaitum ajitendriyaḥ
english: "For this wicked one was formerly cursed when he touched the young woman Rambha; the one of uncontrolled senses is incapable of approaching a woman against her will."

sanskrit: kṣipram eṣyati te bhartā sugrīveṇābhirakṣitaḥ saumitrisahito dhīmāṃs tvāṃ ceto mokṣayiṣyati
english: "Your husband, wise and guarded by Sugriva, will come swiftly with the son of Sumitra and will free you from this torment."

sanskrit: svapnā hi sumahāghorā dṛṣṭā me 'niṣṭadarśanāḥ vināśāyāsya durbuddheḥ paulastyakulaghātinaḥ
english: "For I have seen in dreams most terrible and ill-omened signs portending the destruction of this evil-minded one, destroyer of the family of Pulastya."

sanskrit: dāruṇo hy eṣa duṣṭātmā kṣudrakarmā niśācaraḥ svabhāvāc chīladoṣeṇa sarveṣāṃ bhayavardhanaḥ
english: "For this night-wanderer is cruel, of corrupt soul, of base deeds, and by his very nature and moral wickedness increases the fear of all beings."

sanskrit: spardhate sarvadevair yaḥ kālopahatacetanaḥ mayā vināśaliṅgāni svapne dṛṣṭāni tasya vai
english: "He who vies with all the gods, his mind struck by Time—I have truly seen in my dream the omens of his destruction."

sanskrit: tailābhiṣikto vikaco majjan paṅke daśānanaḥ asakṛt kharayukte tu rathe nṛtyann iva sthitaḥ
english: "The ten-faced one, anointed with oil, hair dishevelled, sinking into mud, riding again and again in a chariot drawn by asses, as though dancing."

sanskrit: kumbhakarṇādayaś ceme nagnāḥ patitamūrdhajāḥ kṛṣyante dakṣiṇām āśāṃ raktamālyānulepanāḥ
english: "Kumbhakarna and the others too—naked, hair fallen loose, anointed with red garlands and unguents—are dragged toward the southern quarter."

sanskrit: śvetātapatraḥ soṣṇīṣaḥ śuklamālyavibhūṣaṇaḥ śvetaparvatam ārūḍha eka eva vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: "Vibhishana alone, bearing a white parasol, wearing a white turban, adorned with white garlands, mounted a white mountain."

sanskrit: sacivāś cāsya catvāraḥ śuklamālyānulepanāḥ śvetaparvatam ārūḍhā mokṣyante 'smān mahābhayāt
english: "And his four ministers, adorned with white garlands and white unguents, mounted the white mountain—they will be freed from this great peril."

sanskrit: rāmasyāstreṇa pṛthivī parikṣiptā sasāgarā yaśasā pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnāṃ pūrayiṣyati te patiḥ
english: "The earth with its oceans will be encompassed by Rama's weapon, and your husband will fill the entire world with his fame."

sanskrit: asthisaṃcayam ārūḍho bhuñjāno madhupāyasam lakṣmaṇaś ca mayā dṛṣṭo nirīkṣan sarvatodiśaḥ
english: "And I saw Lakshmana too, seated on a heap of bones, eating honey-rice pudding and gazing in all directions."

sanskrit: rudatī rudhirārdrāṅgī vyāghreṇa parirakṣitā asakṛt tvaṃ mayā dṛṣṭā gacchantī diśam uttarām
english: "And you I saw more than once, weeping, your limbs wet with blood, guarded by a tiger, going toward the northern quarter."

sanskrit: harṣam eṣyasi vaidehi kṣipraṃ bhartṛsamanvitā rāghaveṇa saha bhrātrā sīte tvam acirād iva
english: "You will attain joy, O daughter of Videha, quickly reunited with your husband; Sita, you will be with the son of Raghu and his brother before long."

sanskrit: iti sā mṛgaśāvākṣī tac chrutvā trijaṭāvacaḥ babhūvāśāvatī bālā punar bhartṛsamāgame
english: Hearing Trijata's words thus, she of the doe-eyed gaze, that young woman, became filled with hope of reunion with her husband.

sanskrit: yāvad abhyāgatā raudrāḥ piśācyas tāḥ sudāruṇāḥ dadṛśus tāṃ trijaṭayā sahāsīnāṃ yathā purā
english: Meanwhile the fearsome and utterly dreadful she-demons returned and saw her seated with Trijata, just as before.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca tatas tāṃ bhartṛśokārtāṃ dīnāṃ malinavāsasam maṇiśeṣābhyalaṃkārāṃ rudatīṃ ca pativratām
english: Markandeya said: Then, that devoted wife afflicted by grief for her husband, wretched, wearing soiled garments, adorned only with the remnant of her jewels, weeping—

sanskrit: rākṣasībhir upāsyantīṃ samāsīnāṃ śilātale rāvaṇaḥ kāmabāṇārto dadarśopasasarpa ca
english: —being attended by rakshasis, seated on a flat rock, Ravana, tormented by the arrows of desire, saw her and drew near.

sanskrit: devadānavagandharvayakṣakiṃpuruṣair yudhi ajito 'śokavanikāṃ yayau kandarpamohitaḥ
english: He who is unvanquished in battle by gods, danavas, gandharvas, yakshas, and kimpurushas went to the Ashoka grove, bewildered by Kandarpa the god of love.

sanskrit: divyāmbaradharaḥ śrīmān sumṛṣṭamaṇikuṇḍalaḥ vicitramālyamukuṭo vasanta iva mūrtimān
english: Wearing divine garments, resplendent, with polished gem-set earrings and a crown of varied garlands, he was like spring embodied.

sanskrit: sa kalpavṛkṣasadṛśo yatnād api vibhūṣitaḥ śmaśānacaityadrumavad bhūṣito 'pi bhayaṃkaraḥ
english: Though adorned with care, he was like a wish-fulfilling tree—yet even so adorned, he was fearsome like a funeral tree at a cremation ground.

sanskrit: sa tasyās tanumadhyāyāḥ samīpe rajanīcaraḥ dadṛśe rohiṇīm etya śanaiścara iva grahaḥ
english: That night-wanderer, approaching near to her of slender waist, appeared beside her like Saturn the slow-moving planet approaching Rohini.

sanskrit: sa tām āmantrya suśroṇīṃ puṣpaketuśarāhataḥ idam ity abravīd bālāṃ trastāṃ rauhīm ivābalām
english: Addressing that beautiful-hipped one, struck by the flower-bannered god's arrow, he spoke thus to the young woman, frightened as the constellation Rohini beset.

sanskrit: sīte paryāptam etāvat kṛto bhartur anugrahaḥ prasādaṃ kuru tanvaṅgi kriyatāṃ parikarma te
english: "Sita, this much has been enough—sufficient favour shown to your husband. Be gracious, O slender one; let your adornment be attended to."

sanskrit: bhajasva māṃ varārohe mahārhābharaṇāmbarā bhava me sarvanārīṇām uttamā varavarṇini
english: "Accept me, O splendid one; wearing ornaments and garments of great worth, be the foremost of all my women, O beautiful one."

sanskrit: santi me devakanyāś ca rājarṣīṇāṃ tathāṅganāḥ santi dānavakanyāś ca daityānāṃ cāpi yoṣitaḥ
english: "I have daughters of gods, and the wives of royal sages; I have daughters of danavas and women of the daityas as well."

sanskrit: caturdaśa piśācānāṃ koṭyo me vacane sthitāḥ dvis tāvat puruṣādānāṃ rakṣasāṃ bhīmakarmaṇām
english: "Fourteen crores of pisachas stand at my command; twice that many man-eating rakshasas of terrible deeds."

sanskrit: tato me triguṇā yakṣā ye madvacanakāriṇaḥ ke cid eva dhanādhyakṣaṃ bhrātaraṃ me samāśritāḥ
english: "Beyond that, three times as many yakshas who carry out my commands—only a few have taken shelter with my brother Kubera, lord of wealth."

sanskrit: gandharvāpsaraso bhadre mām āpānagataṃ sadā upatiṣṭhanti vāmoru yathaiva bhrātaraṃ mama
english: "Gandharvas and apsaras, O auspicious one, O fair-thighed one, always attend upon me when I drink, even as they do my brother."

sanskrit: putro 'ham api viprarṣeḥ sākṣād viśravaso muneḥ pañcamo lokapālānām iti me prathitaṃ yaśaḥ
english: "I am the son of the brahmin sage Vishravas himself; my fame is renowned as the fifth among the guardians of the worlds."

sanskrit: divyāni bhakṣyabhojyāni pānāni vividhāni ca yathaiva tridaśeśasya tathaiva mama bhāmini
english: "Divine foods to eat and drink of all varieties are mine just as they are Indra's, O passionate one."

sanskrit: kṣīyatāṃ duṣkṛtaṃ karma vanavāsakṛtaṃ tava bhāryā me bhava suśroṇi yathā mandodarī tathā
english: "Let the evil karma of forest-dwelling be exhausted for you; be my wife, O beautiful-hipped one, even as Mandodari is."

sanskrit: ity uktā tena vaidehī parivṛtya śubhānanā tṛṇam antarataḥ kṛtvā tam uvāca niśācaram
english: Thus addressed by him, the daughter of Videha, her face beautiful, turned away and placing a blade of grass between herself and him, spoke to that night-wanderer.

sanskrit: aśivenātivāmorūr ajasraṃ netravāriṇā stanāv apatitau bālā sahitāv abhivarṣatī uvāca vākyaṃ taṃ kṣudraṃ vaidehī patidevatā
english: That young woman of exquisitely beautiful thighs, inauspicious in his sight, her two breasts struck together while she continuously rained tears from her eyes—the daughter of Videha, who holds her husband as her god, spoke this word to that wretch.

sanskrit: asakṛd vadato vākyam īdṛśaṃ rākṣaseśvara viṣādayuktam etat te mayā śrutam abhāgyayā
english: "O lord of rakshasas, such words as these have been heard by me—unfortunate that I am—from you speaking not once but many times; and they are filled with degradation."

sanskrit: tad bhadrasukha bhadraṃ te mānasaṃ vinivartyatām paradārāsmy alabhyā ca satataṃ ca pativratā
english: "Therefore, O one fond of the auspicious, may good come to you—turn back your mind; I am another man's wife, unattainable, and ever devoted to my husband."
